title: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
hook: Google splits its fast tier three ways: a workhorse that answers in fewer tokens, a 350-tokens-per-second speed model, and a security specialist locked behind a government pilot.
key_points: Gemini 3.6 Flash is the workhorse tier — Google says it uses 17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash while scoring higher.
Reported gains: DeepSWE 37% → 49%, MLE Bench 49.7% → 63.9%, OSWorld-Verified 78.4% → 83.0%.
3.6 Flash is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 output.
3.5 Flash-Lite is the latency tier: 350 output tokens/second at $0.30 in / $2.50 out per million.
Flash-Lite goes 31% → 54% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and beats the older Gemini 3 Flash on several agentic tasks.
3.5 Flash Cyber finds and fixes security vulnerabilities, shipping only as a limited pilot for governments and trusted partners via CodeMender.
content_html: Google refreshed the fast end of the Gemini lineup with three models at once. Gemini 3.6 Flash is the general workhorse for coding, knowledge work, and multimodal tasks; 3.5 Flash-Lite is the cheap, low-latency option; and 3.5 Flash Cyber is a narrow model for finding and fixing security vulnerabilities, available only to governments and trusted partners in a pilot.
extra_html:
The efficiency pitch

The claim Google leads with for 3.6 Flash isn't a bigger score, it's a shorter answer: 17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash, alongside higher results — DeepSWE 37% → 49%, MLE Bench 49.7% → 63.9%, OSWorld-Verified 78.4% → 83.0%. That framing matters because output tokens are the pricier half of the bill (here $7.50 per million against $1.50 for input) and they set how long you wait for a reply. Reaching the same answer by a shorter route cuts cost and latency together, which compounds in agent loops that make many calls per task.

The speed tier and the specialist

3.5 Flash-Lite targets throughput: 350 output tokens per second at $0.30 in / $2.50 out per million. Google reports it at 54% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, up from 31% for the prior version, and says it beats the older Gemini 3 Flash on several agentic tasks — a small model doing work that used to need a bigger one. 3.5 Flash Cyber is the outlier: tuned for vulnerability detection and repair, described as competitive on the CyberGym benchmark, and gated to a limited-access pilot rather than the API.

3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite are available now through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini Enterprise, and the Gemini app, with Flash-Lite also rolling out in Google Search. Google DeepMind, July 21, 2026.

related.title: Computer Use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
related.hook: DeepMind put computer-use agents — reading the screen, then clicking, typing, and scrolling through real UIs — into its fast, low-cost Flash tier.

related.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier Intelligence That Scales With Your Ambition
related.hook: GPT-5.6 ships as three tiers instead of one model — Luna, Terra, Sol — built around squeezing more capability out of every token rather than just scaling up.

related.title: TUA-Bench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Terminal Agents
related.hook: 120 real terminal tasks — from email triage to PhD-level scientific workflows — show even Claude Opus 4.8 tops out around 66%, far from reliable general computer use.

flashcards.prompt: What is the headline efficiency claim for Gemini 3.6 Flash?

choices.text: It uses 17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash while scoring higher on coding and agentic benchmarks
It generates 350 output tokens per second, the fastest in the lineup
It costs the same per token as 3.5 Flash-Lite

flashcards.explanation_html: Fewer output tokens per answer lowers the bill and the wait even at an unchanged price per token. The 350 tokens/second figure belongs to 3.5 Flash-Lite.

flashcards.prompt: Why does cutting output tokens matter as much as raising benchmark scores?
flashcards.back_html: Output tokens are the pricier half of the bill and set how long you wait for an answer, so a shorter route to the same result cuts both cost and latency.

flashcards.prompt: Which of the three new models is not generally available, and how does it ship?
flashcards.back_html: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber — a limited-access pilot for governments and trusted partners, delivered through CodeMender. 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite are available now.
